key_insight: A spectrally regularized latent compression stage dramatically improves latent flow matching for turbulence by preserving dissipation-range amplitudes that standard MSE-trained VAEs suppress.
engineering_relevance: This enables higher-fidelity synthetic turbulence generation at much lower sampling cost, making generative surrogates more viable for CFD pretraining, uncertainty studies, and data augmentation.
method: Train a VAE with a zone-weighted log-spectral loss instead of plain MSE.
Use the learned latent space inside a flow-matching generator for unconditional turbulence synthesis.
Evaluate whether encoder-side spectral regularization improves high-wavenumber fidelity and cascade statistics.
evidence_signal: On a 256^2 DNS dataset at Re_f≈2250, deep-dissipation retained spectral power improved from 25% to 94% in reconstruction and from 20% to 79% in unconditional generation, with DD bias improving to -0.117 at 20 function evaluations.
watch_item: The paper still reports a residual gap in the magnitude of S_3, suggesting phase-coherent triadic structure is not fully captured yet.
paper_title: Spectrally Regularized Latent Flow Matching for Turbulence Generation
